summary: The Storage section states that transfers live in a month-partitioned transfers table with a covering index on account_id. The rest of the chunk is boilerplate operational claims repeated many times: structured logging with request ids, ninety-day secret rotation via a platform vault, health and readiness endpoints, alerts to the payments channel paging after five minutes, schema review for index impact, a 200 ms p95 read latency target, a three-phase migration over two weekends without downtime, a single YAML config file, low-priority backfills, unit test coverage of parser/validator/posting logic, per-region dashboards, and a spring planning review. No sentence in the chunk contradicts another; the chunk supplies no evidence for any claim.

claims.text: Transfers land in the transfers table, partitioned by month, with a covering index on account_id.
Every write path emits a structured log line with the request id.
Secrets rotate every ninety days through the platform vault.
The service exposes health and readiness endpoints for the orchestrator.
Alerts route to the payments channel and page after five minutes.
Schema changes go through a review that checks index impact.
Latency targets stay under 200 ms at the 95th percentile for reads.
The migration ran in three phases over two weekends without downtime.
Configuration lives in a single YAML file loaded at startup.
Backfills run at low priority so they do not starve live traffic.
Unit tests cover the parser, the validator, and the posting logic.
Dashboards show throughput, error rate, and queue depth per region.
The team reviewed this design in the spring planning cycle.

risks.note: 200 ms p95 read latency target has no source or measurement.
Ninety-day secret rotation and five-minute page delay stated without policy reference.
Migration 'without downtime' over three phases has no evidence or dates.
Sentences repeat verbatim many times; section reads as filler rather than design content.

least_confident: I could not check whether the month partitioning plus account_id covering index on line 3 is consistent with the rest of the document, since this chunk gives no schema or query details.
